draft.title: Scale and maps
card: A map scale such as 1:50 000 means 1 unit on the map is 50 000 of the same unit in real life. So 1 cm on the map is 50 000 cm on the ground.
To find a real distance, measure the map distance and multiply by the second number in the scale. Then change the units to something sensible.
Useful changes: 100 cm = 1 m, 1000 m = 1 km, and 100 000 cm = 1 km. So on a 1:50 000 map, 2 cm on the map is 100 000 cm, which is 1 km.
Worked example: on a 1:25 000 map, two towns are 6 cm apart. 6 × 25 000 = 150 000 cm. Divide by 100 000 to get 1.5 km.
draft.remember: Map length × scale number gives real length. Then change the units.

a.q: On a 1:50 000 map, a walking track measures 4 cm. What is its real length?
a.why: 4 × 50 000 = 200 000 cm. Dividing by 100 000 gives 2 km. The option 200 m comes from dividing by 1000 instead of 100 000, which is a unit mistake.
a.clue: Multiply by 50 000, then change cm to km.

b.q: On a 1:25 000 map, Priya measures 7.2 cm from a campsite to a lake. What is the real distance?
b.why: 7.2 × 25 000 = 180 000 cm. Dividing by 100 000 gives 1.8 km. The option 18 km comes from dividing by 10 000, which mixes up the cm to km change.
b.clue: Multiply by 25 000, then use 100 000 cm = 1 km.
